---
title: "Genomic prediction with masbayes"
---

📐 **Theory:** [Bayesian Alphabet](../../theory/bayesian-alphabet.qmd) ·
[BayesA](../../theory/bayes-bayesa.qmd) ·
[BayesR](../../theory/bayes-bayesr.qmd) ·
[MCMC & EM](../../theory/bayes-mcmc-em.qmd) ·
[Continuous and Binary Trait](../../theory/continuous-and-binary-trait.qmd)

This tutorial fits Bayesian genomic prediction with `masbayes`:
BayesA (Student-$t$ prior, continuous shrinkage) and BayesR (4-class
mixture prior, sparse selection), via both MCMC and EM, on SNP and
phased microhaplotype data. Cross-validation in `masbayes` is **manual**
— the package exposes single-fit functions only — so a worked-out CV
loop is included.

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(masbayes)
library(masreml)         # for evaluate_prediction() — reused on Bayesian GEBVs
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

d <- load_data("large")

y       <- setNames(d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_snp, d$pheno$id)
X_fixed <- stats::model.matrix(~ sex, data = d$pheno)

# Tutorial-scale MCMC params (same as masbayes/examples/04_gwas.R).
# Production runs should use n_iter = 20000, n_burn = 5000, n_thin = 5L.
mcmc <- list(n_iter = 2000L, n_burn = 1000L, n_thin = 5L, seed = 42L)
```
:::


::: {.callout-note}
**Production MCMC**. The chunks below use `n_iter = 2000` for fast
tutorial rendering. For published analyses on real-data scale, use
`n_iter = 20000`, `n_burn = 5000`, `n_thin = 5L` (or longer) and
inspect trace plots before trusting posterior summaries.
:::

## SNP workflow

### Build the design matrix W and wtw

Unlike `masreml`, the Bayesian fitters take a pre-standardised design
matrix $\mathbf{W}$ plus the per-column sum-of-squares $\mathbf{w}'\mathbf{w}$.
`construct_snp_matrix()` returns a list — extract `$W`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
snp_pack <- construct_snp_matrix(d$snp, encoding = "vanRaden")
W_snp    <- snp_pack$W
wtw_snp  <- colSums(W_snp^2)
str(snp_pack)
```


:::
:::


### BayesA — full fit (MCMC)

BayesA assigns each SNP its own variance drawn from a scaled
inverse-$\chi^2$. The marginal prior on $\beta_j$ is Student-$t$ with
heavy tails — markers in real QTL regions are allowed to keep large
effects, while distant markers are shrunk hard.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit_a_mcmc <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_snp,
  y             = y,
  wtw_diag      = wtw_snp,
  X             = X_fixed,
  marker_type   = "snp",
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y) * 0.5,
  method        = "mcmc",
  response_type = "gaussian",
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
  verbose       = FALSE
)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
  labs(x = "SNP index", y = expression(hat(beta)),
       title = "BayesA — posterior-mean SNP effects") +
```

### Predict on held-out candidates


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
train_idx <- d$train_idx
test_idx  <- d$test_idx

fit_a_train <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_snp[train_idx, , drop = FALSE],
  y             = y[train_idx],
  wtw_diag      = colSums(W_snp[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]^2),
  X             = X_fixed[train_idx, , drop = FALSE],
  marker_type   = "snp",
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y[train_idx]) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y[train_idx]) * 0.5,
  method        = "mcmc",
  response_type = "gaussian",
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
```

### BayesA — EM (MAP, faster)

For point estimates without posterior samples, switch `method = "em"`.
EM converges in tens of iterations; MCMC typically wants thousands.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

  w             = W_snp,
  y             = y,
  wtw_diag      = wtw_snp,

  marker_type   = "snp",
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y) * 0.5,
  method        = "em",
  response_type = "gaussian",
```

EM returns the MAP $\hat\beta$ and point estimates of variance
components, but no posterior intervals. Use MCMC when you need
uncertainty quantification (or PIPs, for BayesR).

### BayesR — full fit (MCMC)

BayesR replaces the heavy-tailed continuous prior with a discrete
4-class mixture (zero / small / medium / large). `pi_vec` is the
prior mixture proportions; the conventional starting point is
`c(0.95, 0.02, 0.02, 0.01)`. `sigma2_ah` sets the total genetic
variance scale.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit_r_mcmc <- run_bayesr(
  w             = W_snp,
  y             = y,
  wtw_diag      = wtw_snp,
  X             = X_fixed,
  marker_type   = "snp",
  pi_vec        = c(0.95, 0.02, 0.02, 0.01),
  sigma2_ah     = var(y) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y) * 0.5,
  method        = "mcmc",
  response_type = "gaussian",
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
  verbose       = FALSE
)
```

### Cross-validation (manual loop)

`masbayes` does not provide a `cv_*` wrapper — write the loop
explicitly. The pattern below uses BayesA but swap to `run_bayesr()`
without changing the scaffold (add `pi_vec` / `sigma2_ah`).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(42L)
n      <- nrow(W_snp)
K      <- 5L
folds  <- sample(rep(seq_len(K), length.out = n))

gebv_test  <- rep(NA_real_, n)

for (k in seq_len(K)) {
  tr <- which(folds != k)
  te <- which(folds == k)

  W_tr   <- W_snp[tr, , drop = FALSE]
  wtw_tr <- colSums(W_tr^2)

  fit_k <- run_bayesa(
    w             = W_tr,
    y             = y[tr],
    wtw_diag      = wtw_tr,
    X             = X_fixed[tr, , drop = FALSE],
    marker_type   = "snp",
    nu            = 4.5,
    sigma2_g      = var(y[tr]) * 0.5,
    sigma2_e_init = var(y[tr]) * 0.5,
    method        = "mcmc",
    response_type = "gaussian",
    mcmc_params   = list(n_iter = 1000L, n_burn = 500L, n_thin = 5L,
                         seed = 42L + k),
    verbose       = FALSE
  )

  pred_k <- predict(
    fit_k,
    newdata = W_snp[te, , drop = FALSE],
    X_new   = X_fixed[te, , drop = FALSE]
  )

  gebv_test[te] <- pred_k$GEBV
}
```

### Binary trait

For 0/1 phenotypes, set `response_type = "binary"`. Albert-Chib data
augmentation samples a latent liability variable; the fit object
carries `prob_train` and (after `predict()`) `prob_test` with
$\hat{p}_i = P(y_i = 1)$.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
y_bin <- setNames(as.double(d$pheno$y_bin_qtl_snp), d$pheno$id)

fit_a_bin <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_snp,
  y             = y_bin,
  wtw_diag      = wtw_snp,

  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = 1.0,
  sigma2_e_init = 1.0,
```

## Microhaplotype workflow

For phased microhaplotype data, the design matrix is built with
`construct_wah_matrix()` (W~αh~ coding from Da 2015), and
`marker_type = "multiallelic"` selects the corresponding variance
scaling for $S$ (BayesA) and per-class scaling (BayesR).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
y_mh <- setNames(d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_mh, d$pheno$id)

wah    <- construct_wah_matrix(
  hap_matrix           = d$mh,
  colnames             = attr(d$mh, "block_id"),
  allele_freq_filtered = d$allele_freq
)
W_mh   <- wah$W_ah
wtw_mh <- colSums(W_mh^2)

# BayesA — MCMC
fit_a_mh <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_mh,
  y             = y_mh,
  wtw_diag      = wtw_mh,
  X             = X_fixed,
  marker_type   = "multiallelic",
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y_mh) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y_mh) * 0.5,
  method        = "mcmc",
  response_type = "gaussian",
  mcmc_params   = mcmc,
  verbose       = FALSE
)
```

## Working with the fit object

Key accessors on the returned object:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit_r_mcmc$beta_hat              # posterior-mean marker effects (length p)
fit_r_mcmc$GEBV                  # aggregated total GEBV (length n)
fit_r_mcmc$alpha_hat             # fixed-effect estimates
fit_r_mcmc$h2                    # heritability
fit_r_mcmc$variance_components   # per-class variance posterior
fit_r_mcmc$beta_samples          # MCMC trace, n_kept x p (MCMC only)
```
:::


`summary.masbayes_bayesr` formats these into a one-screen banner;
`predict.masbayes_bayesr(object, newdata, X_new, y_new)` returns the
test-set GEBV and (for binary) `prob`.
